title: Colchicine vs placebo for prevention of pericarditis recurrence
question: In patients with pericarditis, does colchicine added to conventional anti-inflammatory therapy reduce recurrent pericarditis versus placebo? (Double-blind placebo-controlled RCTs.)
pubmed_queries: colchicine AND pericarditis AND (recurrent OR recurrence) AND (randomized OR randomised OR trial)
evidence_base_caveat: The registered PICO is broad (acute first episode OR recurrent pericarditis, treated to prevent recurrence), so ICAP — a first-attack acute-pericarditis trial — is ELIGIBLE and is NOT refused for population. It is not pooled only because its recurrence-specific outcome is not extractable from an accessible source: its abstract reports only the incessant-or-recurrent composite (a different endpoint) and its NEJM full text is not open-access. This pool is therefore the two recurrent-pericarditis trials (CORP and CORP-2), which agree with no between-study heterogeneity and both favour colchicine; the conventional common-effect interval shown alongside the HKSJ interval excludes no-effect, and a later randomised-evidence meta-analysis that includes ICAP reports essentially the same point estimate. The wide HKSJ interval is a two-trial small-sample artefact, not evidence that colchicine is ineffective — adding ICAP (were its recurrence component retrievable) would tighten the interval to exclude no-effect.
comparator_scope_note: The 2012 Heart meta-analysis (PMID 22442198) is a RELATED, BROADER comparator, not a same-scope one: it pooled more trials including open-label studies and mixed primary/secondary prevention (first-attack and recurrent) populations, whereas this review pools double-blind recurrence-outcome trials. Treat the overlap as approximate.
